claude.sample_unit: questions (each answered by 4 LLMs under 2 prompts; 280 responses per prompt)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of LLM responses with vs without child-targeted reading-level prompt
links.effect: FKGL fell from 9.63–11.99 (Prompt A) to 6.36–7.01 (Prompt B); FRE rose from ~42–53 to ~73–77; all p<0.001 across four LLMs.
links.quote: The FKGL decreased by approximately four grades, ranging from 9.63–11.99 to 6.36–7.01.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education with plain-language child-targeted prompt vs adult prompt
links.effect: Prompt B responses had significantly higher readability (FKGL, FRE, syllables/word) for all LLMs (p ≤ 0.001); dominant reading level moved from college/10th–12th grade to 6th–7th grade.
links.quote: Specifically, responses to prompt B exhibit higher readability scores in terms of FKGL, FRE score, average syllables per word, and reading level.

links.outcome: Ophthalmologist-rated potential harm and correctness of LLM myopia education responses
links.effect: About 30% of ChatGPT 4o responses rated slightly harmful; ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini each got 1.14% 'extremely harmful' ratings for Prompt B; authors say clinicians must review all LLM materials.
links.quote: Additionally, approximately 30% of the ChatGPT 4o responses were still rated as “slightly harmful.”

links.outcome: Accuracy, completeness and harm of responses when tailored for children versus adults
links.effect: Prompt A elicited more correct, complete, concise responses than prompt B; ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini were worse on all four metrics under Prompt B (all p<0.02).
links.quote: In general, prompt A elicited more correct, complete, and concise responses from the four language models than did prompt B.

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM response quality across equivalent prompts varying in audience/literacy level
links.effect: Responses differed significantly between adult and child prompts in correctness, completeness, conciseness, and harm for some models (e.g., ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini all p<0.02).
links.quote: Large language models exhibit significant variations in their responses to different prompts ( Figure 4 ).

links.outcome: Poor-quality responses on questions needing clinical judgment
links.effect: Seven of 35 questions received significantly more poor responses; ChatGPT 3.5 had most 'discouraged' ratings, ChatGPT 4o fewest; authors advise LLMs be supplementary, not substitutive.
links.quote: It is crucial to avoid relying solely on LLMs for diagnosis or treatment decisions, ensuring that these AI tools serve a supplementary rather than substitutive role.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering with an audience-specific instruction (child age 8–12) to tailor generative AI education materials

links.effect: ChatGPT 4o led correctness A 91%, B 83%; conciseness A 79%, B 63%; low-harm ratings A 99%, B 97%; all p<0.001.
links.quote: ChatGPT 4o achieved the most positive ratings ("good" and above) in correctness (Prompt A: 91%; Prompt B: 83%) and conciseness (Prompt A: 79%; Prompt B: 63%), as well as the lowest negative ratings in potential harm ratings ("not at all" and "slightly," Prompt A: 99%; Prompt B: 97%) in the generation of educational materials for both adults and children (all p < 0.001).

links.effect: Child prompt reduced FKGL approximately four grades, from 9.63–11.99 to 6.36–7.01.
links.quote: The FKGL decreased by approximately four grades, ranging from 9.63–11.99 to 6.36–7.01.

links.effect: ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini parent-prompt responses outperformed child-prompt responses in all four areas (all p<0.02).
links.quote: When participants responded to prompt A, both ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini outperformed their responses to prompt B in all four areas (all p < 0.02).

links.effect: ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini each received 1.14% “extremely harmful” ratings.
links.quote: Notably, both ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini received 1.14% “extremely harmful” ratings, highlighting the importance of developing safe and reliable AI models.

links.outcome: clinical accuracy and potential harm of child-targeted vs adult-targeted responses
links.effect: Prompt A elicited more correct, complete, and concise responses than Prompt B across models (p < 0.05); ChatGPT 3.5 and Gemini had 1.14% extremely harmful ratings for Prompt B
links.quote: In general, prompt A elicited more correct, complete, and concise responses from the four language models than did prompt B.

screen.practice: reading-level constrained prompting for child-friendly output
screen.reason: The study tests whether adapting the prompt (Prompt A for adults vs. Prompt B for children) alters readability, completeness, conciseness, and potential harm of LLM-generated patient education materials.

primary.practice: prompt engineering for audience reading level
